responsibility.value: Registers FluentValidation into the ASP.NET Core pipeline — enables automatic validation (AddFluentValidationAutoValidation) and discovers all validators from the Application assembly using AnnouncementMappingConfig as the anchor type for assembly scanning.

Owns: Calling AddFluentValidationAutoValidation() to enable automatic model validation on controller action parameters
Calling AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining<AnnouncementMappingConfig>() to register all AbstractValidator<T> implementations from the eNote.Application assembly
doesNotOwn: Individual validator definitions — those live in eNote.Application.Validation as separate AbstractValidator<T> classes discovered by the assembly scan
Validation error formatting or localization — the default FluentValidation ASP.NET Core integration handles error response formatting; this class does not customize it
MediatR pipeline behaviors for validation — no IPipelineBehavior is registered; validation is controller-level only via FluentValidation.AspNetCore

collaborators.detail: Used as the anchor type for AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining to scan eNote.Application for all AbstractValidator<T> classes
AddFluentValidationAutoValidation() is called to wire automatic model validation into the ASP.NET Core MVC pipeline
AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining<T>() is called to register all validators in the scanned assembly

contracts: Every AbstractValidator<T> in the eNote.Application assembly is automatically discovered and registered without per-validator manual wiring
Automatic validation runs on all controller action parameters decorated with [FromBody] or similar model-binding attributes
assumptions: The AnnouncementMappingConfig class is a reliable anchor — it must remain in eNote.Application and must not be moved to another assembly, or validator discovery silently stops

AddFluentValidationAutoValidation() does not conflict with any custom model validation or custom model binding that may also produce error responses — stack-wise, FluentValidation runs before action execution but after model binding
No validator disables automatic validation on specific endpoints via [IgnoreAutoValidation] or similar — all endpoints with model-bound parameters get validated
The default FluentValidation error response format (ProblemDetails with validation errors) is acceptable for the API's consumers
invariants: All validators for request DTOs are in a single assembly (eNote.Application) — no validators exist in other projects
Validation registration is always called during startup service configuration as part of the fluent builder chain in Program.cs
failureModes: If AddFluentValidationAutoValidation() is called but no AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining is configured, no validators are registered and all models pass validation — a silent no-op that looks like everything works but actually provides no validation

If a validator throws an unexpected exception during validation (not a validation failure, but a crash), FluentValidation catches it and may produce a 500 or unexpected error depending on the error-handling middleware order
Multiple assemblies containing validators would require additional AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining calls — this class currently only scans eNote.Application
architecturalNotes: This class represents the FluentValidation integration point — validation conventions for 20+ request validators are all wired through this single registration call.

The choice of AnnouncementMappingConfig as the scan anchor is an arbitrary File → New Item artifact; any class in eNote.Application would work. If AnnouncementMappingConfig is ever deleted, this registration silently stops discovering validators with no compile-time error.
No custom IValidatorInterceptor or IValidatorFactory is registered — all FluentValidation behavior uses default conventions.
Currently no MediatR pipeline validation behavior exists in the codebase — validation is exclusively at the controller/model-binding layer.
